cases.name: Suzanne Clydene "Suzie" Knuth
cases.about: She was a student at Lamar University and an interlibrary loan clerk.
cases.narrative:
Suzanne and her husband, Calvin, were driving home along College Street from the Gateway Shopping Center when their car broke down. Calvin Knuth walked the two miles home to get another car. Suzanne was anxious because they had a dinner party to attend and were running late, so she began walking on the south side of College Street to meet her husband. 

Wicker saw her, abducted her, and drove her out to the Bolivar Peninsula, where he attempted to sexually assault her, but failed. Instead, he strangled her and thinking she was dead, buried her alive. 

Wicker led police to Suzanne Knuth's gravesite 18 days later, on April 22, 1980. He had buried her facedown in a shallow grave between Kaplan and Crystal Beach. An autopsy later revealed she was alive when Wicker left her. She died from
suffocation caused by the sand and debris found in her lungs, according to her autopsy report.
